subject: S22 perf: initial JS 387 KB / AssistantSurface 338 KB — attribution + proposal (need lead decision)
body:
S22 perf budgets: measured on shared @ 53564a9 (vite build --manifest + sourcemaps).

initial JS 386.7 KB gz (limit 250): main 174 + @naadi/shared chunk 110 + supabase 55 + router-core 21 + small.
- main still holds these page modules eagerly (route modules import pages directly, not via lazyPage):
  pathway/PathwayPage + VaultPanel/CostPanel/TaskSheet/StageCard (S17, pathway/routes.tsx)
  settings/SettingsPage, StudyPlanPage, DataExportPage, AppearancePage, AboutPage + planner/StudyPlanSettings (settings routes)
  assistant/SettingsAssistantPage (S14), system/SystemPage + health/HealthPanel, routes/AccountPage/SignInPage/CallbackPage, ink/persist/InkSettingsPage (S21 router.tsx, pending)
  exam/ExamActive + exam/api, practice/api, review/api, notes/api+outbox, learn/api (shell/prefetch imports)
- the @naadi/shared chunk is big because those eager modules import ~80 SDK functions; each SDK call references its
  zod response schema, and zod.gen.ts is one module, so the schemas they reach land in the initial chunk. Tree-shaking
  works (measured: the same 83 names bundled alone = 116 KB gz; zod runtime alone = 27 KB gz). Fix is to make the pages lazy, not to change the generator.
route chunk src/assistant/AssistantSurface.tsx 338 KB gz (limit 150): S14 assistant-ui + markdown stack in one page chunk.

Proposal: once S14/S17/S21 have merged, I (seg22) do one mechanical pass converting the remaining route modules to lazyPage
(no behaviour change; route files only) and re-measure; AssistantSurface split stays with S14 (or lead decides it counts as an
on-demand library surface: it opens from a button, not a route). Keeping the CI gate commit local until both budgets pass.
